verses.text: The word that Yahweh spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, by Jeremiah the prophet.

“Declare among the nations and publish, and set up a standard; publish, and don’t conceal: say, ‘Babylon has been taken, Bel is disappointed, Merodach is dismayed! Her images are disappointed. Her idols are dismayed.’
For a nation comes up out of the north against her, which shall make her land desolate, and no one shall dwell therein. They have fled. They are gone, both man and animal.
“In those days, and in that time,” says Yahweh, “the children of Israel will come, they and the children of Judah together; they will go on their way weeping, and will seek Yahweh their God.
They will inquire concerning Zion with their faces turned toward it, saying, ‘Come, and join yourselves to Yahweh in an everlasting covenant that shall not be forgotten.’

My people have been lost sheep: their shepherds have caused them to go astray; they have turned them away on the mountains; they have gone from mountain to hill; they have forgotten their resting place.

All who found them have devoured them; and their adversaries said, ‘We are not guilty, because they have sinned against Yahweh, the habitation of righteousness, even Yahweh, the hope of their fathers.’
“Flee out of the middle of Babylon! Go out of the land of the Chaldeans, and be as the male goats before the flocks.

For, behold, I will stir up and cause to come up against Babylon a company of great nations from the north country; and they will set themselves in array against her. She will be taken from there. Their arrows will be as of an expert mighty man. None of them will return in vain.
Chaldea shall be a prey. All who prey on her shall be satisfied,” says Yahweh.
“Because you are glad, because you rejoice, O you who plunder my heritage, because you are wanton as a heifer that treads out the grain, and neigh as strong horses;
your mother will be utterly disappointed. She who bore you will be confounded. Behold, she shall be the least of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.
Because of Yahweh’s wrath she won’t be inhabited, but she will be wholly desolate. Everyone who goes by Babylon will be astonished, and hiss at all her plagues.
Set yourselves in array against Babylon all around, all you who bend the bow; shoot at her, spare no arrows: for she has sinned against Yahweh.

Shout against her all around. She has submitted herself. Her bulwarks have fallen. Her walls have been thrown down, for it is the vengeance of Yahweh. Take vengeance on her. As she has done, do to her.

Cut off the sower from Babylon, and him who handles the sickle in the time of harvest. For fear of the oppressing sword, they will each return to their own people, and they will each flee to their own land.
“Israel is a hunted sheep. The lions have driven him away. First, the king of Assyria devoured him, and now at last Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has broken his bones.”
Therefore Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: “Behold, I will punish the king of Babylon and his land, as I have punished the king of Assyria.
I will bring Israel again to his pasture, and he will feed on Carmel and Bashan. His soul will be satisfied on the hills of Ephraim and in Gilead.

In those days, and in that time,” says Yahweh, “the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there will be none; also the sins of Judah, and they won’t be found; for I will pardon them whom I leave as a remnant.
“Go up against the land of Merathaim, even against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod. Kill and utterly destroy after them,” says Yahweh, “and do according to all that I have commanded you.
A sound of battle is in the land, and of great destruction.
How the hammer of the whole earth is cut apart and broken! How Babylon has become a desolation among the nations!
I have laid a snare for you, and you are also taken, Babylon, and you weren’t aware. You are found, and also caught, because you have fought against Yahweh.
Yahweh has opened his armory, and has brought out the weapons of his indignation; for the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, has a work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.
Come against her from the farthest border. Open her storehouses. Cast her up as heaps. Destroy her utterly. Let nothing of her be left.
Kill all her bulls. Let them go down to the slaughter. Woe to them! For their day has come, the time of their visitation.
Listen to those who flee and escape out of the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of Yahweh our God, the vengeance of his temple.

“Call together the archers against Babylon, all those who bend the bow. Encamp against her all around. Let none of it escape. Recompense her according to her work. According to all that she has done, do to her; for she has been proud against Yahweh, against the Holy One of Israel.
Therefore her young men will fall in her streets, and all her men of war will be brought to silence in that day,” says Yahweh.
“Behold, I am against you, you proud one,” says the Lord, Yahweh of Armies; “for your day has come, the time that I will visit you.
The proud one will stumble and fall, and no one will raise him up. I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it shall devour all who are around him.”
Yahweh of Armies says: “The children of Israel and the children of Judah are oppressed together. All who took them captive hold them fast. They refuse to let them go.
Their Redeemer is strong: Yahweh of Armies is his name. He will thoroughly plead their cause, that he may give rest to the earth, and disquiet the inhabitants of Babylon.
“A sword is on the Chaldeans,” says Yahweh, “and on the inhabitants of Babylon, on her princes, and on her wise men.
A sword is on the boasters, and they will become fools. A sword is on her mighty men, and they will be dismayed.
A sword is on their horses, on their chariots, and on all the mixed people who are in the middle of her; and they will become as women. A sword is on her treasures, and they will be robbed.
A drought is on her waters, and they shall be dried up; for it is a land of engraved images, and they are mad over idols.

Therefore the wild animals of the desert with the wolves will dwell there. The ostriches will dwell therein; and it will be inhabited no more forever; neither will it be lived in from generation to generation.
As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and its neighbor cities,” says Yahweh, “so no man will dwell there, neither will any son of man live therein.
“Behold, a people comes from the north; and a great nation and many kings shall be stirred up from the uttermost parts of the earth.
They take up bow and spear. They are cruel, and have no mercy. Their voice roars like the sea. They ride on horses, everyone set in array, as a man to the battle, against you, daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon has heard the news of them, and his hands become feeble: anguish has taken hold of him, pains as of a woman in labor.

Behold, the enemy will come up like a lion from the pride of the Jordan against the strong habitation; for I will suddenly make them run away from it. Whoever is chosen, I will appoint him over it; for who is like me? Who will appoint me a time? Who is the shepherd who can stand before me?”

Therefore hear the counsel of Yahweh, that he has taken against Babylon; and his purposes, that he has purposed against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely they shall drag them away, even the little ones of the flock. Surely he shall make their habitation desolate over them.
At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth trembles; and the cry is heard among the nations.

footnotes.content: A prophet speaks the Lord's word about Babylon—the great power of that hour. Even empires that seem unshakeable are in His hands, and He speaks through those whom the world overlooks.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Publish it among the nations: Babylon's gods are disappointed, her idols dismayed. There's a strange comfort in knowing that all the power earthly kingdoms trust in—wealth, might, the favor of false gods—crumbles before the true God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A nation from the north will make the land desolate—all of it. The Lord can raise up nations and lay them low, and no fortress resists His will. But notice: this judgment clears the way for His people's return.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In that time, Israel and Judah will come weeping, seeking the Lord their God. Even after failure and exile, repentance leads the remnant home. The road back is always open to those who turn toward Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They turn their faces toward Zion, asking to join themselves to the Lord in an everlasting covenant. What grace—to be offered covenant again, after breaking covenant. Zion is not a place of judgment but of homecoming.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lost sheep, scattered by shepherds who led them astray. How tenderly the Lord sees His people's condition—not as rebels alone, but as sheep who've been forgotten their resting place. Even the cause of our wandering matters to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their enemies devoured them and said they had not sinned—smooth faces and lying words. But there's a truth under all this: Israel's God is the habitation of righteousness, the hope of their fathers. That hope does not die.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Flee out of Babylon! Leave the land of the Chaldeans. Sometimes the Lord calls His people to movement, to courage, to step away from captivity's comfort. He does not leave them there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A company of great nations from the north will come against Babylon with arrows that will not return in vain. The judgment is sure, the outcome fixed. In all this thunder, the Lord is at work for His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Chaldea becomes prey, and those who plunder her will be satisfied. Even spoil and ruin are in His hand. Nothing escapes His sight or His sovereignty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You rejoice and neigh like strong horses, glutted with the plunder of My heritage. The Lord sees those who gloat over His people's captivity, and their gladness will be turned to shame.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your mother will be utterly disappointed, she who bore you will be confounded. Babylon, once mighty, will become the least of nations—a wilderness, a dry land. Pride goes before ruin, as it always has.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Because of the Lord's wrath she won't be inhabited but wholly desolate. All who pass will hiss at her plagues. There is a terrible silence in an empty city—the absence of glory where glory once stood.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Set yourselves in array, all who bend the bow—shoot at her, spare no arrows, for she has sinned against the Lord. The command is given; the work of judgment unfolds. Justice is real and exacts its cost.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: She has submitted. Her bulwarks have fallen. Her walls are thrown down—it is the vengeance of the Lord. As she has done, so it is done to her. The Lord's justice is exacting but measured.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cut off the sower from Babylon, and him who handles the sickle in the time of harvest. When the seed of life stops, desolation follows. No planting, no reaping—a land gone silent and still.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Israel is a hunted sheep—first devoured by the king of Assyria, now broken by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. The pattern is clear: weakness invites the predator. But a sheep that belongs to the Lord is never finally lost.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord of Armies will punish the king of Babylon and his land as He punished the king of Assyria. The same justice visits every tyrant. The Lord does not forget the harm done to His flock.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will bring Israel again to his pasture—Carmel and Bashan, the hills of Ephraim and Gilead. Real places, good land where the people will feed and be satisfied. The Lord restores to the people what belonged to them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In that time the iniquity of Israel will be sought and found no more, and their sins likewise—I will pardon them whom I leave as a remnant. Forgiveness is complete and radical. A new covenant begins with those who return.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Go up against the land of Merathaim and against Pekod—destroy them utterly. The judgment is specific, concrete, real. The Lord knows the names and places where injustice has taken root.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A sound of battle in the land and of great destruction. The noise of war fills the air—armies, chariots, death. This is the audible reality of judgment, no longer distant or silent.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: How the hammer of the whole earth is cut apart and broken! Babylon, the instrument of power, becomes broken. The Lord can shatter what seemed unshatterable.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I have laid a snare for you, and you are taken—you didn't even know it was happening. There's an invisible hand at work, setting traps that close with precision. The arrogant never see it coming.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord has opened His armory and brought out the weapons of His indignation. The Almighty has a work to do, and He possesses everything needed to accomplish it. His arsenal is inexhaustible.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Come against her from the farthest border, open her storehouses, cast her up as heaps—destroy utterly. Nothing remains. The destruction is total, leaving only rubble where once stood pride.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kill all her bulls—woe to them, for their day has come. Even the symbols of strength are slaughtered. Power means nothing when the day of visitation arrives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Listen to those who flee and escape from Babylon—they will declare in Zion the vengeance of the Lord. Survivors will carry word of His justice back to His holy city. The Lord's name will be vindicated.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Babylon has been proud against the Lord, against the Holy One of Israel. Pride against the Almighty is the only true rebellion. And it will be repaid according to what she has done.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Her young men will fall in her streets, and all her men of war will be brought to silence. The noise of battle ends in a terrible quiet. Strength brings only death when it stands against the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I am against you, you proud one—your day has come. The Lord declares Himself the enemy of pride. When the Almighty is against a kingdom, no shield avails.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The proud one will stumble and fall, and no one will raise him up. Fire will be kindled in his cities and devour all around. Isolation in judgment—no rescue, no reprieve.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The children of Israel and Judah are oppressed together—all who took them captive hold them fast. The Lord sees His captive people held in iron grip. He does not forget their bondage.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their Redeemer is strong—the Lord of Armies. He will plead their cause and give rest to the earth, bringing disquiet to Babylon. The oppressed have an advocate whose strength is infinite.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A sword is on the Chaldeans, on Babylon's inhabitants, her princes, her wise men. No rank escapes the judgment. The sword takes the counsel as well as the common soldier.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A sword is on the boasters—they will become fools. A sword is on her mighty men—they will be dismayed. Boasting and strength are leveled together before the Lord's judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A sword is on their horses, their chariots, all their mixed people—they will become as women. Even the instruments of war are stripped of power. Treasures are robbed, defenses stripped bare.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A drought is on her waters—they will be dried up. A land of idols and those mad over them will lose even the comfort of water. The judgment touches the very springs of life.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wild animals and wolves will dwell there; ostriches will inhabit it. Never again will it be lived in from generation to generation. Where once stood cities and commerce, only beasts and emptiness remain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and its neighbors, so no man will dwell there. The comparison is stark: Babylon, like those cities of old, will be erased by divine justice. The pattern of judgment repeats.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A people comes from the north, and great nations and many kings shall be stirred up from the uttermost parts of the earth. The Lord gathers the nations to His purpose—instruments of judgment, drawn from far and near.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They are cruel, have no mercy—their voice roars like the sea. They ride on horses, set in array. The armies are relentless and terrible. Yet they are the Lord's hand, not their own.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The king of Babylon has heard the news, and his hands become feeble—anguish takes hold like a woman in labor. Even the mighty are unmade by fear when judgment approaches. There is no peace for the wicked.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The enemy will come up like a lion from the Jordan pride against the strong habitation. The Lord will suddenly make them flee—He appoints whom He chooses. The shepherd question is rhetorical: who is like Him? Who can stand before His presence?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hear the counsel of the Lord against Babylon—surely they will drag away even the little ones of the flock. The desolation is complete. Not a person escapes, not a child remains. Babylon's habitation becomes a ruin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth trembles and the cry is heard among the nations. Readers today hear an echo of how the Lord moves through history—great nations rise and fall, and the news of His justice reverberates across the world. His judgment is never merely local or forgotten.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
